records.c: One-based driving-stage file number. The controller increments this after the interstitial and dispatches the ending at $0B instead of loading another driving stage.
Receives the file number in A and block count in Y. Blanks the display, calls $0646 and returns on carry set. On error it flashes the border and polls both joystick fire lines before retrying.

Stores one output byte at ($68),Y. The surrounding loop moves backwards through destination pages. Carry selects literal bytes from the input bitstream or a copy from the backward reference at $64/$65.

Saves the banking and stack pointer, sets $01 to $35, establishes the drive handshake and resets the bitstream reader. Dispatches $0500 to unpack the requested blocks and restores the port and stack before returning.

Patches the common road drawing operands with this map's table addresses, installs the script and scenery pointers, zeros the accumulated score and initial progress fields, sets five missiles and builds the five starting traffic lanes.
Polls pause, advances road messages, motion and traffic, clears the inactive screen and renders the road and objects. It waits for the raster tick before committing timer and sprite ordering data.
Toggles $0A, selects the new screen-page high byte from $927C and calls the colour-row copier. Loops to $0890 while $A7C5 and $A7BB are clear.
Fourteen dashboard screen codes copied to $F3B2 by the first-stage setup. The wording is BORDER, a digit placeholder, and MILES. The space and digits use the dashboard font at $E800.
The 127 little-endian dispatch and operand words for round 1. $7A1F jumps through the word indexed by twice $12. The opening $7A33 takes the next word, $0C62, as the initial scenery stream pointer.
Increments $A7C9 and $12, then tail-calls the next script entry.
Decrements the digit in $F3B9. Clears the plural suffix cell at the one-mile glyph and replaces the remaining label from $79F1 when the digit reaches zero.
Round 1 scenery descriptor pointer table with 14 entries. Indices 0–8 point into the engine. Indices 9–13 point into this stage. $8EBC reads a pointer after scaling the object type by two.

Toggles $A7D0 and advances the road script. Exchanges the glyph colour and both road-band pointer pairs with the three stored alternatives, then swaps 1,584 glyph bytes with VIC RAM from $F9C8.
Three addresses saved by the exchange. They are the glyph colour lookup and the two road band tables for the active surface after the next swap.
Road surface glyph bytes exchanged with $F9C8–$FDC7. After the exchange this region keeps the glyph bytes of the alternate surface for the next call.
Road surface glyph bytes exchanged with $FDC8–$FFF7. After the exchange this region keeps the glyph bytes of the alternate surface for the next call.

Eight forty-byte rows of glyph values. $8C86 uses this base when selecting the alternate height band and advances the source by 80 bytes per displayed row. The glyph values index the colour table at $262F.
First four raw rows from the second band source patched into $8D34/$8D35. $8C0E selects a clipped phase and $8CF9 turns the glyph values into both screen and colour bytes.
Round 1 maps each road glyph index to its colour RAM value here. The stage prologue patches this base into $8D03/$8D04 and $9109/$910A for the road-band and scenery blitters.

Uses $A766 to select a little-endian pointer from $27BB and calls $89FE while that actor is active. Subtracts the distance step from $A754 and dispatches removal below $3F. With no active actor it dispatches by $A7C2.

Walks five traffic slots backwards, adjusts the lateral positions within bounds, and can move a nearby leading vehicle to the opposite lane. Dispatches per-vehicle data via the pointer table at $27BB.

Tests five normal traffic slots and one extra actor slot for the visible depth range. Projects each position with a factor from $9BEF in an eight-step shift-and-add loop, then assigns the resulting sprite data through the primary object arrays.
Alternate sprite bank 1, shape indices $00–$0F. Index 1 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C000–$C3FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 1, shape indices $10–$1F. Index 1 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C400–$C7FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Continues the first alternate lower sprite bank, from shape index $14 through $1F. This subrange is exchanged with $C500–$C7FF by $9B76.
Alternate sprite bank 1, shape indices $20–$2F. Index 1 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C800–$CBFF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 1, shape indices $30–$33. Index 1 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $CC00–$CCFF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 2, shape indices $00–$0F. Index 2 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C000–$C3FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 2, shape indices $10–$1F. Index 2 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C400–$C7FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 2, shape indices $20–$2F. Index 2 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $C800–$CBFF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 2, shape indices $30–$33. Index 2 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $CC00–$CCFF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 3, shape indices $88–$97. Index 3 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $E200–$E5FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 3, shape indices $98–$A7. Index 3 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $E600–$E9FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 3, shape indices $A8–$AF. Index 3 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $EA00–$EBFF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 4, shape indices $88–$97. Index 4 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $E200–$E5FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 4, shape indices $98–$A7. Index 4 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $E600–$E9FF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.
Alternate sprite bank 4, shape indices $A8–$AF. Index 4 at $9B76 exchanges these 64-byte slots with $EA00–$EBFF for VIC use. The old shape bytes return to this range.

The loaded file originally executes JSR $AC00. The setup at $AC47 replaces that opcode with BIT so the trainer patch routine runs on the initial entry and the later handoff skips another call. Then the handoff disables interrupts and enters the stage controller at $A842.
Writes three digits at $F34B-$F34D from the low digit in $A7D3 and the high and low nibbles of $A7D2. Adding $9C converts the values to dashboard glyphs.
Looks up the two timing words using the indices at $A740 and $A741. Subtracts $17 from the second word for timer A's latch and stages four background colour values in $E1-$E4.
Sets the steering index to four, seeds three parallel sprite lanes and starts physical sprite zero at X=$AE and Y=$96 with shape $69 in both screen buffers.
Fills the twenty top rows of the colour buffer at $AC00 with eight. Then copies two hundred dashboard colour bytes from $F720-$F7E7 to $DB20-$DBE7.
Reads $DC01 through $A8FD. If the value is exactly $7F it waits through release, press and release of the selected keyboard row while calling the tick wait at $727B.
Compares the requested effect index in A with $A7D6 unless $BC38 is set. On an accepted request, records the new index and copies the selection byte from $6BA9 into $BBF9.

Tests active-low CIA1 port A bit 4. Starts an effect on the initial press, increments the hold counter towards ten when missiles remain, and changes sprite zero's pointer to the missile sight at the threshold.

Decrements the short fire timer if active. A hold counter of ten selects sprite $6D, decrements the missile stock, erases its HUD glyph and requests sound effect nine. Clears the hold counter after the release.

Checks the steering lock at $A791 and reads active-low left and right from $DC00. Sets lateral increments of +3 or -3, adjusts the steering animation index and bounds the new position computed at $6F0A.
Tests active-low up on CIA1 port A. Under the fuel gate at $6F46, the normal acceleration path spends two units from the fractional fuel byte and calls $70E3 up to the normal speed threshold.
Tests active-low down on CIA1 port A and calls the speed-decrease path at $7189 when pressed.
If the turbo countdown is zero, tests the signed POTX sample and the $EF value of CIA1 port B. With fuel remaining, queues the engaged flag and effect, then loads the countdown with $32.
While fuel remains, uses 24 fractional fuel units per update, decrements the turbo countdown and raises speed by up to four, with a cap of $70.
Draws three values from $A7AF and the two nibbles of $A7B0 as two-by-two glyph blocks using $71AA. Recolours two fourteen-cell panel scales when $A7C0 changes.

Adds A to the packed decimal value at $A738 and refreshes the digits. On a decimal carry, changes the leading digit and clears the following two. Otherwise increments the separate $A737 accumulator and adds a sprite lane entry for each threshold of fourteen.
Converts the high and low nibbles of $A738 to digit glyphs by adding $9C and writes them at $F35E-$F35F.
Jumps to the loop at $A915 which waits for the byte at $0B to change. The raster IRQ at $93A9 increments that byte.
Zeros the four pages at $D400-$D7FF under the current banking and clears the zero-page bytes from $02 to $FF, preserving the processor port.
Selects VIC bank $C000 with CIA2 port A, sets $D016 to $18, enables all eight sprites and sets their multicolour bits and shared colours.
Shifts the two state bytes at $0C/$0D, XORs them and adds $0D using the carry from the shifts before storing the new low byte.
Adds the speed byte at $A7A4 into the substep accumulator. Uses its upper bits for the whole distance step at $A7A2, then keeps only the lower six bits as the next substep remainder.
Clears $A749-$A7D9, calls the common SID and zero-page clear, installs the initial vertical and panel values and fills the initial arrays with fixed-step sequences.

Installs the gameplay vectors at $932E, initializes the player and the sound player, prepares panel fields, clears two HUD message slots, and prepares the sprite list before jumping into its stack-based ordering code.
Writes $FE to three effect request slots, programs the play video bank, enables CPU interrupts and enables both CIA2 timer interrupts and CIA1 timer A.
Tests four thresholds at $7940 against $A73A and sets the corresponding cells of the panel row beginning at $F357 using offsets from $7944.

Rotates among seven pending message bits in $A7CC, copies the chosen fourteen glyphs to $F3DA and starts a ten-tick display counter. A value of five blanks the row. Some messages also request an effect.
Doubles the script index at $12 and reads a little-endian address from the table at ($0E),Y. Jumps through $10/$11 after clearing $13.
Increments the script index and loads a scenery-record pointer into $2C/$2D. Resets its byte offset at $2E, increments the script index again and dispatches the next entry.
Copies 48 bytes of traffic state from $A749 to $7CA6, saves $A78F, clears six vehicle type slots and several motion-state counters, sets $A7BF and advances the script.
Selects three pointer pairs from the $835E, $8370 and $8382 curves while the segment counter is below nine. Supplies negative lateral and geometry steps, then advances the script.
Selects follow-up geometry from $8394, $83A8 and $83BC for ten segment counts, then clears both lateral steps and advances the script.
Similar three-table road curve update using $83D0, $83E2 and $83F4. Sets positive lateral and geometry steps for the first nine counts.
Updates the three geometry pointers from $8406, $841A and $842E for ten counts before clearing both geometry steps and dispatching.
Advances the script when the segment counter at $13 reaches $10.
Advances the script when the segment counter at $13 reaches $20.
Advances the script when the segment counter at $13 reaches four.
Zeros the road script index and initializes parallel projection and road lookup pointers before falling into $8BF9.
Dispatches the first road script command, fills the first four scenery slots by calling $8DE3 for indices zero through three and leaves three in the slot index at $2B.

Chooses a height row or a clipped case from signed $A746. Patches the destination operands for the two screen buffers and combines the horizontal band offset with the current stage's source address at $8D34. Clips the subsequent blit height.
Selects the other road band based on signed $A746 minus seven. Computes source and destination operands for $8CF9 using the stage's $8D32 pointer and clips the blit height.

Writes forty source glyphs per row into the selected screen and uses each glyph as an index into a colour lookup. Steps both destination row addresses by forty and the stage's source by eighty for the next displayed row.
The operand bytes following the indexed load at $8D02 hold the stage's glyph-to-colour lookup address. The stage's first routine patches them.
Two little-endian road-band pointers set by the stage prologue. The second is the initial source operand used by $8C0E when selecting the horizontal phase of a band.
Adds the signed road increment at $A78E to $A7A0. Stores the sum below forty and wraps to zero or thirty-nine at the edges.

Subtracts the distance step at $A7A2 from four slot offsets. Wraps negative offsets by sixteen and reads a new record. Types three and six alter palette or timing while their offsets drive the two timing lookup tables.

Reads three values via $2C/$2D and an offset in $2E into parallel arrays starting at $A794, $A798 and $A79C. $FE steps back to the previous record and $FF enters the reset path. Types three and six swap the alternate colour and timing settings.

Sets up projection scratch values from the selected object and multiplies the magnitude of the player-plus-camera offset by a table factor in an eight-step shift-and-add loop. Restores the sign before consulting the pointed object table.
Checks the motion threshold before queuing the crash animation and its sound. Clears several motion, display and pending message flags and refreshes the panel values.
Clips a projected row's left and right ends to the forty-column display. Combines the column with row lookup data, patches the two destination operands, and copies nonzero row bytes through ($06),Y.
The indexed load at $9108 uses this stage-specific pointer to turn each scenery glyph into a colour RAM byte.
High-byte table shared between the band blitter and the object-row copier. Each adds a base page for the selected buffer.
Copies a sequence of 40-column colour rows from the buffer at $AC00 to colour RAM beginning at $D800, with complete row passes indexed backwards.
Clears the upper twenty rows of one 40-column screen. $0A selects $F000 or $F400. Each pass writes the same column of all twenty rows, leaving their dashboard rows outside the clear.

Masks IRQs, restores $2F/$35 to the CPU port, clears both CIA interrupt masks and acknowledges their pending bits. Disables VIC interrupt sources, clears SID volume and acknowledges pending VIC flags.
Writes hardware IRQ $9392 and NMI $9365 with the KERNAL banked out. Selects $93DC as the first raster dispatch target, enables the VIC raster interrupt and stops both timers on each CIA.

Preserves A in $E0 and reads CIA2's interrupt flags. Timer A chooses the first pair of background colour values and the other CIA timer path chooses the second pair. The unflagged path writes one to $A7BB.
Saves A to the IRQ restore operand and samples CIA1's flags. The VIC arm saves X and Y, acknowledges the raster interrupt and dispatches through the self-modified JMP at $93A6.
Selects the dashboard character base through $D018, clears background and sprite enable values, advances the frame signal $0B, and schedules the $93DC raster handler for line $128.
Restarts the timed display events, latches sprite-zero collisions, calls the music and effects ticks, then uses sorted object indices to load sprite Y, X, pointer, colour, priority and high-X bits.
If the interval is usable, selects the raster handler for the next time sprite one can be programmed. The branch at $97EB programs the new slot.
Copies the scheduled object’s X and Y, shape, colour and priority into physical sprite one. Stores the shape in both screen pointer tables.
Copies five parallel 21-byte arrays into zero-page lanes $54, $69, $7E, $93 and $A8. Temporarily alters the CIA1 port setup while reading SID POTX into $A7C8.

Uses the page-one stack as an ordered bucket array. Each object supplies its Y byte, shifted right once to choose a stack offset. The unrolled insertion loop scans for a negative free marker and stores the object's index.

Handles an active hit according to sprite zero's sight or projectile shape. Shape $6C subtracts one from the selected vehicle strength. Larger weapon shapes subtract four. A negative result replaces that traffic slot with the destruction state, increments the packed BCD award counter and requests an effect.
Selects two addresses and a page count from the five parallel tables beginning at $9BC8. Patches four direct indexed operands, exchanges the two byte arrays a page at a time and restores X.
Source high bytes for the exchanges at $9B76. Entries one through four select $3B00, $4800, $5500 and $5F00.
Low bytes for the source operands in the page exchange. The first entry uses the no-op location $9031.
The destination high bytes for A=1–4 are $C0, $C0, $E2 and $E2 respectively.
Low bytes for the exchanges. A=1–4 use page-aligned operands.
Each exchange decrements the selected count after copying a complete page. Entries one and two exchange 13 pages each. Entries three and four exchange 10 pages each.
Copies four pages each of screen and colour data and 32 pages of bitmap data from the loaded buffers, selects VIC bank $4000 and sets up a multicolour bitmap with sprites disabled.
Copies a page indexed by Y, increments the source and destination high-byte operands, then repeats until X has decremented past zero.
Coarse fuel counter. When the fractional byte at $A73B borrows, the accelerator and turbo paths decrement this byte and refresh the fuel marks.
Low byte of the fuel reserve. Normal acceleration at $6F54 subtracts two and turbo at $6FCB subtracts $18 from this low byte.
Engine speed byte. The distance accumulator at $7793 consumes it, and the turbo path at $6FF4 limits it to $70.
Turbo starts at $32 and decrements once each driving update through $6FD8. Fuel exhaustion clears it at $7007.
Initializes the first or trainer-selected stage, then calls the stage entry at $0801. Dispatches the result in $A7BB to the two failure pictures or the success and next-stage path.

Waits for 128 ticks, loads interstitial file number $0432 plus $0E, displays it and waits for fire. Increments the stage counter and calls the loader with four blocks, except at stage $0B where it branches to the ending loader.
The startup instruction restores $D011 before replacing its own first opcode with RTS. The capture in play holds the replacement opcode.
Writes one to $0432 for an unmodified start. If the trainer's $02AF differs from one, computes twice the selected value minus one and jumps to the next-stage load path.

Uses Y and resets the stack to the appropriate value before handing off to either the running stage's continuation or the initial display startup. The stage controller patches the continuation low byte.

Applies the release's initial timing and optional trainer patches by rewriting operands and entry opcodes in the driving engine. $AC47 changes the first instruction at $6900. This routine survives in the hand-over snapshot and the normal gameplay colour buffer overwrites it.
Twenty-three timing words copied over the game's timing table at $69EE by the conditional start-up path at $AC16.
Decrements the immediate countdown and jumps to $B003. On expiry reloads the counter and returns. Start-up can patch the raster handler to call this divider.
Uses forty-byte source rows from $AD40 onward to update the lower road colour rows. The start-up wrapper can patch the normal colour-copy routine to jump here.
Indirect entry by JMP to $B06F, which resets two voice state lanes, zeros SID register offsets $00-$17 and initializes the filter and volume register.
Entry JMP to $B0AA. Called by the raster handler before the effects tick at $BBF4.
Moves the SID cutoff byte one step toward its target at $B062. If the fade flag is set, decreases the volume nibble every twenty calls. Dispatches the two voice lanes through $B10D.

Receives a logical voice index in X and the SID register lane offset in Y. Advances the voice's divider and duration, enters the event reader on expiry and uses instrument settings to update its waveform and pitch. The disabled path clears the gate register and returns.
Embedded PETSCII credit naming the Saudi tune and Marc Francois. The following credit names Sean Connolly's music player.
Consumes the request slot at $BBF7+X, looks up the effect stream and duration via $BE42 and $BE62, resets per-voice flags and clears the SID control and envelope lane before effect playback.
Sixteen 64-byte sprite slots with shape indices $00–$0F in VIC bank $C000. Each shape starts with 21 rows of three bytes and leaves the 64th byte outside the displayed shape.
Second byte of sprite slot zero in the currently installed low sprite set. The displayed shape includes this byte and the asset selector can test it before exchanging sets.
Sixteen shape slots $10–$1F in the loaded sprite set. The bank-relative pointer is the slot number and the VIC multiplies it by 64.
Shape slots $20–$2F use RAM $C800–$CBFF. The stage’s object placement code passes shape indices to the raster sprite allocator.
Four final shape slots in the stage’s low-bank sprite block, from $30 at $CC00 to $33 at $CCC0.
Twelve shared sprite slots $34–$3F above the low-bank stage sprite set. The visible forms include left, centre and right car-body panels.
Sixteen sprite slots $40–$4F under I/O. The rendered atlas shows car body sections, damage fragments and flames in this group.
Sixteen slots $50–$5F in RAM beneath the SID register mirrors. The intermediate explosion shapes in the sprite atlas use these slots.
Sixteen slots $60–$6F in RAM beneath colour RAM. Slots $69–$6C show the small sight, bracketed sight and sparks. The release-fire branch selects the explosion at $6D.
Sixteen slots $70–$7F behind the CIA register addresses. The stack-sorted sprite multiplexer addresses them via the same $C000 image bank.
Sprite area for VIC indices $88–$97, sixteen 64-byte slots. The raster multiplexer writes the shape indices of scheduled objects to both pointer tables.
Shape slots $98–$A7 continue the second stage sprite block. Slots $A0–$A7 also occupy the first half of the character memory selected by the dashboard split.
This address is 32 bytes into sprite slot $A2 and is in the lower half of the dashboard font address space too.
Eight sprite slots $A8–$AF in the last two pages of the replacement upper sprite block.
The dashboard letters begin in the second half of the charset based at $E800. Glyph $80 is blank, $81–$9A display A–Z, $9B is a dot and $9C–$A5 display 0–9.
Five panel cells cleared from the right when the release branch at $6DD6 spends a missile. The clearing value is the blank glyph $80.
Two hundred authored colour bytes copied to the bottom five screen rows of colour RAM, starting at $DB20.
Main scene character set. The timed write of $CE to $D018 in VIC bank $C000 selects this 2 KB glyph base for the road portion of the screen.
Stage 1 replaces the road character set starting at glyph $39. This segment reaches the penultimate complete glyph slot and the opening byte of slot $FF.
Upper half of the road character set. Groups of eight bytes give the timed road display its cell rows. The load’s final byte is at $FFF8 and the CPU uses the final hardware vector bytes separately.
The hardware NMI vector points to $9365 once $932E installs the gameplay vectors.
The hardware IRQ vector points to $9392 with KERNAL ROM banked out.
